slide.heading: Sugar
slide.subheading: Insulin, glucagon, and the diabetes you'll treat your whole career

nodes.label: Muscle and fat take up glucose (GLUT4)

lines.text: Good morning, I'm Jonah Weiss, endocrinology. About one American adult in ten has diabetes, and many more have prediabetes. Whatever you specialize in, you'll manage it.
Today: how the β cell senses glucose, what insulin and glucagon do, the two main kinds of diabetes, and the drugs.

slide.heading: How the β cell senses glucose
bullets: Glucose enters through GLUT2; glucokinase traps it
More ATP closes K-ATP channels
The cell depolarizes; Ca²⁺ channels open
Ca²⁺ triggers insulin release
Sulfonylureas close K-ATP directly

lines.text: Glucose enters the β cell through GLUT2 and glucokinase phosphorylates it: remember glucokinase's high Km from the fall? This is where it matters.
As glucose is burned, ATP rises and closes ATP-sensitive potassium channels. The cell depolarizes, voltage-gated calcium channels open, and calcium triggers insulin release.
Sulfonylureas skip the glucose step and close those channels directly, which is why they can cause hypoglycemia.

slide.heading: Insulin and glucagon
bullets: Insulin: GLUT4 to the surface of muscle and fat
Insulin: glycogen, fat and protein built
Insulin: lipolysis and ketones switched off
Glucagon: glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis, ketones
C-peptide: released with the body's own insulin

lines.text: Insulin is the hormone of the fed state. It sends GLUT4 transporters to the surface of muscle and fat cells, and tells the liver to store glycogen and stop making glucose.
Just as important, it switches off fat breakdown, and with it ketone production.
Glucagon does the opposite in fasting: it releases glucose from glycogen, makes new glucose, and lets the liver make ketones.
Insulin is made as proinsulin, and the C-peptide is cut off and released with it. That gives you a way to tell the body's own insulin from injected insulin.

slide.heading: Type 1, type 2, and the diagnosis
bullets: Type 1: autoimmune β-cell loss; no insulin
Type 2: insulin resistance, then β-cell failure
HbA1c ≥ 6.5%, or fasting glucose ≥ 126 mg/dL
2-h OGTT ≥ 200, or random ≥ 200 with symptoms
HbA1c: the average of about three months

lines.text: Type one is autoimmune: the immune system destroys the β cells, usually in young people, and without insulin they make ketones.
Type two is far commoner: tissues resist insulin, the β cells work harder, and over years they fail. Obesity and family history are the big risks.
We diagnose with any of these, confirmed on a repeat test unless the picture is unmistakable.
The HbA1c is glucose stuck to hemoglobin. Red cells live about four months, so it reflects the last two to three.

slide.heading: Diabetic ketoacidosis
bullets: No insulin: unchecked glucose and ketone production
Anion-gap metabolic acidosis; deep, fast breathing
Osmotic diuresis: severe dehydration
Treat: fluids, insulin infusion, potassium
Check potassium before starting insulin

lines.text: Without insulin, fat breaks down unchecked and the liver pours out ketones: diabetic ketoacidosis.
The blood becomes acidic with a raised anion gap, and the patient breathes deeply and fast to blow off carbon dioxide.
Glucose spills into the urine and drags water with it, so they're profoundly dehydrated.
Treatment is fluids, an insulin infusion, and potassium. Here's the trap.

slide.heading: The drugs
bullets: Metformin: less glucose from the liver; first line
Metformin: GI upset; rare lactic acidosis; B12
SGLT2 inhibitors: glucose out in the urine
SGLT2: genital infections; heart and kidney benefit
GLP-1 agonists: more insulin with meals, weight loss

lines.text: Metformin is first line for most people with type two diabetes. It mainly reduces the liver's glucose output, doesn't cause hypoglycemia on its own, and is cheap.
SGLT2 inhibitors block glucose reabsorption in the proximal tubule, from the renal lecture, so glucose leaves in the urine. They also protect the heart and kidneys.
The glucose in the urine is why they cause genital yeast infections.
GLP-1 receptor agonists boost insulin release only when glucose is high, suppress glucagon, slow the stomach and help with weight loss.
